title: Attention as a Routing Graph: Live Circuit Extraction from a Single Forward Pass
abstract: arXiv:2609.25285v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Finding circuits in language models usually means running many careful interventions. We try something simpler: treat attention as a routing map from one forward pass, keep a small set of routes that point toward the answer, and ask whether those routes actually matter.   They often do. On induction and IOI (tasks where the "right" circuit is already known), ablating our extracted edges hurts the model much more than ablating a random set of the same size. We evaluate n=100 prompts per cell on GPT-2 Small, GPT-2 Medium, and Pythia-410M, with paired gap tests and bootstrap confidence intervals. The extract step costs one forward; a head-by-head patch sweep costs about two orders of magnitude more.   We are not claiming a complete circuit atlas. We are claiming a cheap sketch that carries real causal signal on known tasks, with clear failure modes when it does not. Code and evaluation artifacts are at https://github.com/Aquinf03/live-cir

translated_title: 注意力作为路由图：从单次前向传播中提取活性电路
translated_abstract: 在语言模型中寻找电路通常意味着进行大量细致的干预实验。我们尝试了一种更简单的方法：将注意力视为单次前向传播得到的路由图，保留一小组指向答案的路由，并检验这些路由是否真的重要。它们往往确实重要。在归纳和IOI（这些任务的“正确”电路已知）任务上，消融我们提取的边对模型的损害远大于消融同等数量的随机边。我们在GPT-2 Small、GPT-2 Medium和Pythia-410M上对每个单元格评估n=100个提示，并使用配对差距检验和自助法置信区间。提取步骤只需一次前向传播；而逐头修补扫描的成本大约高出两个数量级。我们并不声称提供完整的电路图谱，而是提供一种廉价的草图方法，它在已知任务上携带真实的因果信号，并且在失效时有明确的失败模式。代码和评估工件见 https://github.com/Aquinf03/live-cir
tldr: 该论文提出将注意力机制视为路由图，仅通过单次前向传播即可低成本提取语言模型中的电路，在已知电路的任务上其提取边的消融效果显著优于随机消融，且成本比传统逐头修补扫描低约两个数量级。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes treating attention as a routing graph to extract circuits from language models in a single forward pass, showing that ablating the extracted edges hurts performance far more than random ablation on known tasks, at roughly two orders of magnitude lower cost than head-by-head patch sweeps.
